claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit. To do this properly, I'll need to gather some information about you and your children.

Let me start with a few basic questions:

**Could you please tell me the name and age of the child or children you'd like to claim Child Benefit for?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Yes, I'd like to find out if I can claim for my son Alex. He's 16 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I'd like to understand your situation a bit better.

**Does Alex currently live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. That's helpful to know.

**Is Alex in full-time education or training, or does he have any other circumstances I should know about (for example, is he unemployed, disabled, or in any other situation)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, he recently left school actually. But he's just signed up with the local careers service to figure out what he wants to do next.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I appreciate you letting me know that. Before I can give you a final answer, I need to check the specific eligibility rules around this situation.

Let me look up the current Child Benefit eligibility requirements to make sure I give you accurate information.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that context. I can see from the eligibility rules that this is an important detail. According to the rules, when a child is 16 or over, you can normally still qualify for Child Benefit if they stay in approved education or training. However, there's also a provision for children who leave education or training.

**I need to clarify: When Alex registered with the careers service, did they provide him with a formal registration or confirmation from the careers service? And do you know if he's registered as a jobseeker with the jobcentre as well?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he registered with the careers service properly. They gave him confirmation when he signed up. He hasn't registered with the jobcentre though - just the careers service.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for clarifying that. Based on the information you've provided, let me review the eligibility rules carefully.

According to the Child Benefit eligibility rules, you can continue to claim Child Benefit for a 16 or 17 year old who leaves education or training and registers with a government-sponsored careers service. Alex has done exactly that - he's registered with the local careers service and has confirmation of his registration.

The rules state you can claim Child Benefit for up to 20 weeks while he's in this situation after leaving school.

However, before I give you my final assessment, let me just confirm one more thing:

**Is there anything else about Alex's circumstances I should know - for example, is he in any paid work, or does he receive any benefits in his own right?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at all right now, and he doesn't get any benefits himself.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent. I now have all the information I need to assess your eligibility.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Great news! You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:

Alex is 16 years old and has recently left school. The rules allow you to continue claiming Child Benefit for 20 weeks when a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training and registers with a government-sponsored careers service. Since Alex has properly registered with the local careers service and has confirmation of his registration, he meets this requirement perfectly.

Additionally, there are no disqualifying factors - he's not working 24 hours or more per week, and he's not receiving any benefits in his own right.

You should be able to apply for or continue your Child Benefit claim for Alex during this 20-week period while he works with the careers service to plan his next steps.

If you have any other questions or circumstances change, it's always a good idea to inform the Child Benefit Office so they have the most up-to-date information.
